149	def export_batch(path: str, after: int = 0, limit: int = 100) -> bytes:
150	    """Return one replication batch of audit records as UTF-8 JSON bytes.
151	
152	    Selects the first ``limit`` records whose ``seq`` is greater than
153	    ``after``.  ``after`` must not exceed the log's last seq (an empty or
154	    missing log has last seq 0); otherwise :class:`ValueError` is raised.
155	
156	    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError` (``bool`` is not accepted as
157	    an int); ``after < 0`` or a ``limit`` outside ``[1, 1000]`` raises
158	    :class:`ValueError`.  A corrupt log raises
159	    :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.CorruptAuditError` and filesystem
160	    errors propagate as :class:`OSError`.  The log is never modified.
161	    """
162	    if not isinstance(path, str):
163	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
164	    if isinstance(after, bool) or not isinstance(after, int):
165	        raise TypeError("after must be an int")
166	    if isinstance(limit, bool) or not isinstance(limit, int):
167	        raise TypeError("limit must be an int")
168	    if after < 0:
169	        raise ValueError("after must be >= 0")
170	    if limit < _MIN_LIMIT or limit > _MAX_LIMIT:
171	        raise ValueError("limit must be in [1, 1000]")
172	
173	    all_records = audit.read(path)
174	    last_seq = all_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if all_records else 0
175	    if after > last_seq:
176	        raise ValueError("after must not exceed the last audit seq")
177	
178	    selected = [record for record in all_records if record[audit.SEQ] > after]
179	    selected = selected[:limit]
180	    batch_records = [
181	        {key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS} for record in selected
182	    ]
183	
184	    next_seq = batch_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if batch_records else after
185	    batch = {
186	        AFTER: after,
187	        COMPLETE: next_seq == last_seq,
188	        NEXT: next_seq,
189	        RECORDS: batch_records,
190	        VERSION: _BATCH_VERSION,
191	    }
192	    ordered = {key: batch[key] for key in _BATCH_KEYS}
193	    text = json.dumps(ordered, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
194	    return text.encode("utf-8")
195

197	def _invalid_batch(message: str) -> ValueError:
198	    return ValueError(f"invalid replication batch: {message}")

201	def _compact(obj: object) -> bytes:
202	    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")

204	
205	def _parse_batch(batch: bytes) -> dict:
206	    """Validate a batch against the export byte contract and decode it."""
207	    if not batch.endswith(b"\n") or batch.endswith(b"\n\n"):
208	        raise _invalid_batch("must be a single JSON object terminated by one LF")
209	    try:
210	        data = json.loads(batch[:-1].decode("utf-8"))
211	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
212	        raise _invalid_batch("is not valid UTF-8 JSON") from exc
213	
214	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or tuple(data.keys()) != _BATCH_KEYS:
215	        raise _invalid_batch(
216	            "top-level object must have exactly the keys "
217	            "'after', 'complete', 'next', 'records', 'version' in order"
218	        )
219	    version = data[VERSION]
220	    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int) or version != _BATCH_VERSION:
221	        raise _invalid_batch("version must be the integer 1")
222	    for key in (AFTER, NEXT):
223	        if isinstance(data[key], bool) or not isinstance(data[key], int):
224	            raise _invalid_batch(f"{key} must be an int")
225	        if data[key] < 0:
226	            raise _invalid_batch(f"{key} must be >= 0")
227	    if not isinstance(data[COMPLETE], bool):
228	        raise _invalid_batch("complete must be a bool")
229	    records = data[RECORDS]
230	    if not isinstance(records, list):
231	        raise _invalid_batch("records must be a list")
232	    if len(records) > _MAX_LIMIT:
233	        raise _invalid_batch("records must contain at most 1000 items")
234	    if not records and not data[COMPLETE]:
235	        raise _invalid_batch("empty records require complete to be true")
236	
237	    expected_seq = data[AFTER]
238	    expected_prev = audit._ZERO_HASH if data[AFTER] == 0 else None
239	    for index, record in enumerate(records):
240	        if not isinstance(record, dict) or tuple(record.keys()) != _RECORD_KEYS:
241	            raise _invalid_batch(
242	                f"record {index} must have exactly the keys "
243	                "'detail', 'hash', 'kind', 'prev', 'seq', 'source' in order"
244	            )
245	        # Only the byte contract is enforced here: key order, the
246	        # seq/prev/hash chain and the stored values.  Value-domain rules
247	        # (non-empty fields, the kind enum) belong to audit.append's event
248	        # input, so records from any log audit.read accepts stay importable.
249	        prev = record[audit.PREV]
250	        digest = record[audit.HASH]
251	        if expected_prev is not None:
252	            if prev != expected_prev:
253	                raise _invalid_batch(
254	                    f"record {index} prev does not match the previous record hash"
255	                )
256	        elif not isinstance(prev, str) or not _HEX64.fullmatch(prev):
257	            # The first record's prev refers to the exporter's log and
258	            # cannot be checked against local state; require hash shape.
259	            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} prev must be 64 lowercase hex chars")
260	        seq = record[audit.SEQ]
261	        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int):
262	            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} seq must be an int")
263	        expected_seq += 1
264	        if seq != expected_seq:
265	            raise _invalid_batch(
266	                f"record {index} seq is {seq}, expected {expected_seq}"
267	            )
268	        without_hash = {
269	            audit.DETAIL: record[audit.DETAIL],
270	            audit.KIND: record[audit.KIND],
271	            audit.PREV: prev,
272	            audit.SEQ: seq,
273	            audit.SOURCE: record[audit.SOURCE],
274	        }
275	        if digest != audit._record_hash(without_hash):
276	            raise _invalid_batch(f"record {index} hash does not match its contents")
277	        expected_prev = digest
278	
279	    expected_next = expected_seq if records else data[AFTER]
280	    if data[NEXT] != expected_next:
281	        raise _invalid_batch("next must be the last record seq, or after when empty")
282	
283	    # The bytes must be the exact canonical compact encoding export_batch
284	    # produces: no whitespace, no non-canonical escapes, fixed key order.
285	    if _compact(data) + b"\n" != batch:
286	        raise _invalid_batch("encoding is not the canonical compact form")
287	    return data

290	def _restore_log(path: str, existed: bool, size: int) -> None:
291	    """Best-effort rollback of a failed append.
292	
293	    Append-mode writes only ever extend the file, so truncating back to
294	    the pre-call size restores the exact prior bytes; a file the failed
295	    call newly created is unlinked again.  Rollback errors are swallowed
296	    so the original :class:`OSError` propagates unchanged.
297	    """
298	    try:
299	        if existed:
300	            with open(path, "r+b") as handle:
301	                handle.truncate(size)
302	                handle.flush()
303	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
304	        else:
305	            os.unlink(path)
306	    except OSError:
307	        pass

310	def import_batch(path: str, batch: bytes) -> dict:
311	    """Validate a replication batch and append its suffix to the local log.
312	
313	    See the module docstring for the byte contract.  A ``path`` that is not
314	    a str or a ``batch`` that is not bytes raises :class:`TypeError`; any
315	    contract violation raises :class:`ValueError`.  The local log is read
316	    solely through :func:`audit.read`, and a corrupt log or filesystem
317	    error propagates as :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.
318	    CorruptAuditError` or :class:`OSError`.  Any failure leaves the log
319	    byte-identical to its pre-call state (still missing when it was
320	    missing).
321	    """
322	    if not isinstance(path, str):
323	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
324	    if not isinstance(batch, bytes):
325	        raise TypeError("batch must be bytes")
326	
327	    data = _parse_batch(batch)
328	    after = data[AFTER]
329	    batch_records = data[RECORDS]
330	
331	    local_records = audit.read(path)
332	    last_seq = local_records[-1][audit.SEQ] if local_records else 0
333	
334	    if after > last_seq:
335	        return {NEED: [last_seq + 1, after], NEXT: last_seq, STATUS: STATUS_MISSING}
336	
337	    # Records with seq <= last_seq must already exist locally and match the
338	    # batch record field by field; everything past last_seq is appended.
339	    suffix: list[dict] = []
340	    for record in batch_records:
341	        seq = record[audit.SEQ]
342	        if seq <= last_seq:
343	            local = local_records[seq - 1]
344	            if any(record[key] != local[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS):
345	                raise _invalid_batch(
346	                    f"record {seq} conflicts with the local record of the same seq"
347	                )
348	        else:
349	            if seq != last_seq + 1 + len(suffix):
350	                raise _invalid_batch("records past the local last seq must be contiguous")
351	            suffix.append(record)
352	
353	    if not suffix:
354	        return {NEED: None, NEXT: max(last_seq, data[NEXT]), STATUS: STATUS_DUPLICATE}
355	
356	    # The first appended record must chain onto the local log's last hash
357	    # (or the zero hash for an empty log).
358	    local_last_hash = local_records[-1][audit.HASH] if local_records else audit._ZERO_HASH
359	    if suffix[0][audit.PREV] != local_last_hash:
360	        raise _invalid_batch(
361	            "first new record prev must match the local last record hash"
362	        )
363	
364	    lines = b"".join(
365	        audit._encode_line({key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS})
366	        for record in suffix
367	    )
368	    existed = os.path.exists(path)
369	    original_size = os.path.getsize(path) if existed else 0
370	    dir_fd: int | None = None
371	    try:
372	        with open(path, "ab") as handle:
373	            handle.write(lines)
374	            handle.flush()
375	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
376	        if not existed:
377	            dir_fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
378	            os.fsync(dir_fd)
379	    except OSError:
380	        _restore_log(path, existed, original_size)
381	        raise
382	    finally:
383	        if dir_fd is not None:
384	            os.close(dir_fd)
385	
386	    return {NEED: None, NEXT: max(last_seq, data[NEXT]), STATUS: STATUS_APPLIED}

436	def _validated_apply_request(
437	    request: object,
438	) -> tuple[str, str, dict, dict]:
439	    """Validate an apply_remote request into (id, source, base, remote).
440	
441	    The states come back as fresh copies obeying the merge state contract,
442	    so type errors raised while validating them stay :class:`TypeError`.
443	    """
444	    if not isinstance(request, dict):
445	        raise TypeError("request must be a dict")
446	    if set(request.keys()) != set(_REQUEST_KEYS):
447	        raise ValueError(
448	            "request must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'source', 'base' "
449	            "and 'remote'"
450	        )

452	    source = request[SOURCE]
453	    if not isinstance(request_id, str):
454	        raise TypeError("request id must be a str")
455	    if request_id == "":
456	        raise ValueError("request id must be non-empty")
457	    if not isinstance(source, str):
458	        raise TypeError("request source must be a str")
459	    if source == "":
460	        raise ValueError("request source must be non-empty")
461	    base_clock, base_records = merge._validated_state(request[BASE])
462	    remote_clock, remote_records = merge._validated_state(request[REMOTE])
463	    base = {merge.CLOCK: base_clock, merge.RECORDS: base_records}
464	    remote = {merge.CLOCK: remote_clock, merge.RECORDS: remote_records}

468	def _request_digest(request_id: str, source: str, base: dict, remote: dict) -> str:
469	    """SHA-256 of the canonical compact encoding of the logical request."""
470	    ordered = {
471	        BASE: {merge.CLOCK: base[merge.CLOCK], merge.RECORDS: base[merge.RECORDS]},
472	        ID: request_id,
473	        REMOTE: {
474	            merge.CLOCK: remote[merge.CLOCK],
475	            merge.RECORDS: remote[merge.RECORDS],
476	        },
477	        SOURCE: source,
478	    }
479	    payload = json.dumps(
480	        ordered, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
481	    ).encode("utf-8")
482	    return _digest(payload)

516	def _parse_ledger(raw: bytes) -> tuple[dict, dict[str, str], list[dict]]:
517	    """Validate every byte of a ledger into (state, requests, audit).
518	
519	    Any decoding, structural, state, index or chain violation raises
520	    :class:`ValueError`; in particular a type fault in the stored state is
521	    an on-disk corruption, not a :class:`TypeError`.
522	    """
523	    try:
524	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
525	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
526	        raise _ledger_invalid("is not valid UTF-8") from exc
527	    try:
528	        data = json.loads(text)
529	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
530	        raise _ledger_invalid("is not valid JSON") from exc
531	
532	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
533	        raise _ledger_invalid("must be a JSON object")
534	    if set(data.keys()) != set(_LEDGER_TOP_KEYS):
535	        raise _ledger_invalid(
536	            "must contain exactly the keys 'audit', 'requests', 'state' "
537	            "and 'version'"
538	        )
539	    version = data["version"]
540	    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int):
541	        raise _ledger_invalid("version must be an int")
542	    if version != LEDGER_VERSION:
543	        raise _ledger_invalid("version must be the integer 1")
544	
545	    try:
546	        clock, records = merge._validated_state(data[STATE_KEY])
547	    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
548	        raise _ledger_invalid(f"state is invalid: {exc}") from exc
549	    state = {merge.CLOCK: clock, merge.RECORDS: records}
550	
551	    raw_requests = data[REQUESTS]
552	    if not isinstance(raw_requests, dict):
553	        raise _ledger_invalid("requests must be a JSON object")
554	    requests: dict[str, str] = {}
555	    for bound_id, bound_digest in raw_requests.items():
556	        if not isinstance(bound_id, str) or bound_id == "":

686	def _record_decision(
687	    local_clock: dict,
688	    local_record: list | None,
689	    remote_record: list,
690	) -> tuple[str, dict | None]:
691	    """Classify one remote record against the current local state."""
692	    need = merge._remote_need(remote_record, local_clock)
693	    if need:
694	        return STATUS_MISSING, need
695	    if local_record is None:
696	        return APPLY, None
697	    if local_record == remote_record:
698	        return STATUS_DUPLICATE, None
699	    if merge._dominates(remote_record[2], local_record[2]):
700	        return APPLY, None
701	    if merge._dominates(local_record[2], remote_record[2]):
702	        return STALE, None
703	    return CONFLICT, None

706	def _overall_status(decisions: list[str]) -> str:
707	    """Overall outcome with missing > conflict > stale > applied > duplicate.
708	
709	    Any ``missing``/``conflict``/``stale`` item dominates; otherwise the
710	    request applies as soon as at least one item applies (the rest being
711	    apply or duplicate), and a batch with nothing to do is duplicate.
712	    """
713	    for status in (STATUS_MISSING, CONFLICT, STALE):
714	        if status in decisions:
715	            return status
716	    return STATUS_APPLIED if APPLY in decisions else STATUS_DUPLICATE

790	def _reserve_tmp_file(path: str) -> tuple[BinaryIO, str]:
791	    """Open a fresh, uniquely named transaction file next to ``path``.
792	
793	    Exclusive binary create (``"xb"``) atomically reserves a random name
794	    and gives the file the same mode a plain create would; a collision
795	    simply retries.  The returned open binary handle owns the file until
796	    the caller closes it.
797	    """
798	    last_error: OSError | None = None
799	    for _ in range(128):
800	        tmp_path = f"{path}.tmp.{os.urandom(8).hex()}"
801	        try:
802	            return open(tmp_path, "xb"), tmp_path
803	        except FileExistsError as exc:
804	            last_error = exc
805	    raise last_error if last_error is not None else OSError(
806	        "could not reserve a ledger temporary file name"
807	    )

810	def _link_predecessor_aside(path: str) -> str:
811	    """Hard-link the existing ledger to a unique backup name.
812	
813	    ``os.link`` is atomic and fails with :class:`FileExistsError` when the
814	    candidate name already exists (for example as a leftover of a killed
815	    transaction), so the name can be reserved by the link itself without
816	    any create-then-link window.
817	    """
818	    last_error: OSError | None = None
819	    for _ in range(128):
820	        backup_path = f"{path}.old.{os.urandom(8).hex()}"
821	        try:
822	            os.link(path, backup_path)
823	        except FileExistsError as exc:
824	            last_error = exc
825	            continue
826	        return backup_path
827	    # Practically unreachable: 128 random 64-bit name collisions in a row.
828	    raise last_error if last_error is not None else OSError(
829	        "could not reserve a ledger backup file name"
830	    )

833	def _atomic_write(path: str, payload: bytes) -> None:
834	    """Durably replace ``path`` with ``payload`` as a single transaction.
835	
836	    Every transaction uses *unique* file names (an exclusively created
837	    ``path + ".tmp.<random>"`` temporary and a random-suffixed hard link
838	    for the predecessor), so a fixed ``path + ".tmp"``/``path + ".old"``
839	    leftover from an older interrupted process never collides with a
840	    fresh commit.  Such fixed leftovers are internal artifacts: they are
841	    never read as a ledger and are swept best-effort before the
842	    transaction starts -- a sweep failure cannot block the commit, which
843	    never depends on those names.
844	
845	    The temporary file's write, flush and file sync, the replacement and
846	    the following directory sync all lie inside the boundary.  An existing
847	    predecessor is retained as a hard link -- without ever removing
848	    ``path`` -- until the new file is installed and the directory has
849	    synced, so any :class:`OSError` rolls back by renaming that link back:
850	    the prior file returns byte-for-byte (as the same inode, with no
851	    rewriting and therefore no dependence on a working fsync or free
852	    space), and a path the call created is removed again.  The rollback
853	    syncs the directory as well.  The original :class:`OSError` propagates
854	    unchanged.  On success both the file and the directory have been
855	    synced; the unique backup link's removal (and the matching directory
856	    sync) is best-effort and never undoes a commit.
857	    """
858	    existed = os.path.exists(path)
859	    # Retained fixed-name artifacts from earlier interrupted calls are
860	    # internal, never read as a ledger, and must never stand in the way of
861	    # a fresh transaction; the transaction itself uses unique names.
862	    _remove_quietly(path + ".tmp")
863	    _remove_quietly(path + ".old")
864	
865	    tmp_handle, tmp_path = _reserve_tmp_file(path)
866	    backup_path: str | None = None
867	    stage = "write"
868	    try:
869	        with tmp_handle as handle:
870	            handle.write(payload)
871	            handle.flush()
872	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
873	        if existed:
874	            backup_path = _link_predecessor_aside(path)
875	            stage = "link"
876	        stage = "install"
877	        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
878	        stage = "sync"
879	        storage._fsync_dir(path)
880	    except BaseException:
881	        _rollback_ledger_write(path, tmp_path, backup_path, existed, stage)
882	        raise
883	
884	    # The new ledger is durable from this point on; the retained
885	    # predecessor link is internal cleanup only.  Its removal (and the
886	    # matching directory sync) is best-effort and never undoes a commit.
887	    if existed and backup_path is not None:
888	        _remove_quietly(backup_path)
889	        try:
890	            storage._fsync_dir(path)
891	        except OSError:
892	            pass

1065	    versions, secret formats and validity periods raise
1066	    :class:`ValueError`.

1069	        raise TypeError("keyring must be a dict")

1071	    for node, entries in keyring.items():
1072	        if not isinstance(node, str):

1082	            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
1083	                raise TypeError(f"{where} must be a dict")

1087	                    "'secret', 'notBefore', 'notAfter' and 'revoked'"

1097	                )

1105	                )
